mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which typically leads to reduced corporate revenue growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST < 850 and RSAFS < 400000.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply shock, indicated by industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 90, manufacturing output contraction leads to higher input costs and reduced corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 90.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 3.5% indicates accelerating inflation, which typically triggers aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, leading to higher real interest rates and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 130000 thousand persons) indicates an exceptionally tight labor market, which typically fuels consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS > 130000.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP level (GDPC1) below its 10-year average indicates a recessionary economic environment, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 is below its 10-year average.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which typically increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.
